title: Meet the ESP32
short: The ESP32 is a tiny, powerful microcontroller with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth built in.

title: Flash two LEDs
short: Your first circuit: two LEDs that take turns, like the lights at a level crossing.

title: Guard the fridge
short: Left the fridge open again? A reed switch is a pair of springy contacts in a glass tube that touch when a magnet comes close.

title: Use Wi-Fi
short: The ESP32 can join your Wi-Fi and serve a tiny web page.

title: Sound a siren
short: A passive buzzer clicks every time its pin flips; flip it hundreds of times a second and you hear a note.

title: Build a mini piano
short: Eight of the ESP32’s pins can feel a fingertip. Wire each one to a copper key and the board plays a note with tone() when you touch it — no…

title: Fill a ring of LEDs
short: A potentiometer is a resistor with a slider: turning it moves its OUT pin anywhere from 0 V to 3.3 V, and the ESP32’s 12-bit ADC reads that as 0…

title: Make a mood lamp
short: An RGB LED is three LEDs — red, green and blue — in one.

title: Light up in the dark
short: A light-dependent resistor (LDR) lets more current through the more light falls on it.

title: Distance meter
short: A pocket tape measure with no tape. The HC-SR04P times an ultrasonic echo, and a little OLED screen on its own stand shows the distance in big…

title: Drive a wheel
short: A pin can’t power a motor, and a single transistor can only turn it one way.

title: Laser barrier gate
short: A red laser shines across the road onto a receiver.

title: Talk over Bluetooth
short: No router needed: the ESP32 can pair with your phone directly.

title: Board to board
short: ESP-NOW lets ESP32 boards message each other directly: no router, no pairing, and a message lands in milliseconds.

title: Smart parking bay
short: Put it all together. The distance sensor watches a parking bay, a traffic light guides the driver in — green, then yellow, then red to stop — and…

title: Automatic water pump
short: A tank that fills itself. A probe in the lid measures the water; at the low mark the ESP32 clicks a relay that runs a mains pump, and at the high…

title: Keypad door lock
short: Type the right code and the safe opens. A keypad is a grid of buttons wired in rows and columns: the ESP32 drives one column at a time and listens…

title: Sun-tracking solar panel
short: A solar panel makes the most power when it faces the sun, so this one turns to follow it.

title: Ultrasonic radar
short: An HC-SR04P tells you how far away something is, but only straight ahead.

title: Pick and place
short: A stepper motor doesn’t just spin: every pulse turns it exactly one step, 200 to a turn.

title: Traffic light
short: A three-lamp module cycles red → green → amber; a crossing button and buzzer for pedestrians.

title: Weather station
short: BME280 temperature, humidity and pressure on I2C, shown live on a 0.96" OLED sharing the same bus.

title: Robot car
short: Two DC motors through a DRV8833 on a 6 V battery pack; an HC-SR04 (with a 1k/2k divider on ECHO) makes it back away from walls.

title: Keypad door lock
short: Type 1234 on the keypad: the servo bolt opens, the green LED lights and the buzzer chirps. A wrong code flashes red.

title: AI camera
short: Camera Module 3 on CAM0 and the 13 TOPS AI Kit on PCIe run YOLO object detection; the Active Cooler keeps the SoC from throttling.

title: Blink (ESP32)
short: The hello-world of hardware: one LED and a 330 Ω resistor on GPIO2.

title: Blink (Pi 5)
short: gpiozero LED on GPIO17 (physical pin 11) through a 330 Ω resistor.

title: Motion alarm
short: A PIR sensor wakes a buzzer and LED when someone walks past.

title: Plant monitor
short: A capacitive soil probe on ADC1 (GPIO34) with the reading on an OLED; a red LED asks for water.

title: Night light
short: The Pi 5 has no ADC, so an MCP3008 reads a light-dependent resistor divider over SPI and turns an LED on in the dark.

title: Servo dial
short: Turn the potentiometer and the servo follows — analogRead on ADC1 mapped to 0–180°.

title: NeoPixel mood ring
short: Twelve WS2812B pixels driven from SPI MOSI (GPIO10) — the reliable way on Pi 5 — with a button to change the effect.
